36 In the circuits shown, the batteries are identical and all have negligible internal resistance. All of
the resistors have the same resistance. The diodes have zero resistance when conducting and
infinite resistance when not conducting.
In which circuit is the current in the battery greatest?
A
B
C
D

hints: Look at the triangle direction of each diode in circuits A, C and D and decide which branches are forward-biased to conduct and which are reverse-biased to block.
Count the number of conducting resistor branches in parallel in each circuit - recall two resistors of resistance $R$ in parallel give $R/2$.
Apply $I = V/R_{total}$ with the same battery e.m.f. $V$ to compare a total of $R/2$ against a total of $R$ or an open circuit.
walkthrough: Let the battery e.m.f. be $V$ and each resistor be $R$. A conducting ideal diode adds $0$ resistance, a non-conducting diode gives infinite resistance and opens that branch.
In circuit A both diodes point the same way for forward conduction, so both middle and right branches each have resistance $R$ and both conduct.
Two equal resistors in parallel give $1/R_{total} = 1/R + 1/R$, so $R_{total} = R/2$. Battery current is $I = V/R_{total} = 2V/R$.
In circuit B the two diodes in the one series loop point in opposite senses, so one must be reverse-biased and the series current is zero.

In circuit C the left branch with no diode conducts with $R$, but the right branch diode is reversed and blocked, so $R_{total} = R$ and $I = V/R$. In circuit D the two diodes oppose, so only one parallel branch conducts, again $R_{total} = R$ and $I = V/R$.
Comparing $2V/R$ with $V/R$ and zero shows the smallest conducting resistance gives the greatest current. This is option A.

A.explanation: Both parallel branches have forward-biased diodes so both conduct, giving $R/2$ total resistance and current $I = 2V/R$, the largest.

B.explanation: The two diodes in the single series loop oppose each other so one is reverse-biased and blocks all current.

C.explanation: Only the plain resistor branch conducts because the diode branch is reverse-biased, giving total resistance $R$ and smaller current than two parallel conducting branches.

D.explanation: The two diodes oppose each other so only one parallel branch conducts, giving total resistance $R$ and current $V/R$.
